title: sati sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en:
At Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell aware and clearly comprehending. This is our instruction to you.

And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu aware?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells observing the body as body, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.

… vedanā as vedanā, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
… mind as mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
… phenomena as phenomena, ardent,
clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is aware.

And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu clearly comprehend?
Here, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu
vedanā are understood as they arise,
understood as they remain present,
understood as they pass away.

Thoughts are understood as they arise,
understood as they remain present,
understood as they pass away.
Perceptions are understood as they arise,
understood as they remain present,
understood as they pass away.
It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu clearly comprehends. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell aware and clearly comprehending. This is our instruction to you.”
